questions.q: Why is a silent retrieval failure especially dangerous in a RAG pipeline?
options: It always crashes the application
It can produce a confident-sounding answer built on irrelevant context, which is often worse than no answer at all
It permanently deletes the affected chunks
It automatically triggers re-ranking twice
questions.explain: When retrieval fails without the pipeline noticing, the model can still produce a fluent answer from weak or irrelevant context, which looks trustworthy without actually being grounded.

questions.q: What happens with a nearest-neighbor vector search when no truly relevant content exists in the collection?
options: It throws an error and halts the pipeline
It automatically triggers a clarifying question
It returns zero results every time
It still returns a top_k list of the closest available vectors — just with low similarity scores
questions.explain: A nearest-neighbor search returns something whenever top_k > 0, even if nothing in the collection is a genuinely good match — which is why a raw result list alone doesn't prove relevance.

questions.q: What does a score_threshold do when used as a failure-detection mechanism?
options: It increases the embedding dimensionality
It re-ranks results by relevance_score instead of similarity
It treats any result below a minimum similarity score as effectively not a match, letting the pipeline respond honestly instead of using a weak chunk
It deletes low-scoring chunks from the vector database permanently
questions.explain: A score_threshold catches the clearest failure case — nothing relevant exists — by letting the pipeline recognize that a low score isn't a usable match.

questions.q: Why can't a score threshold alone catch every retrieval failure?
options: Thresholds are only supported by one vector database vendor
A moderately-scored chunk can still pass the threshold without actually answering the question, producing a fluent but subtly wrong answer
Thresholds only work with fixed-size chunking
Thresholds disable the re-ranking step entirely
questions.explain: A chunk can be related enough to clear the threshold while still not containing the actual answer, which is a harder failure mode a simple score cutoff can't catch.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what are the three honest responses once a retrieval failure is detected?
options: Abstain, ask a clarifying question, or widen the search
Retry the same query twice and average the scores
Always fabricate a best-guess answer to avoid an empty response
Delete the user's query from the logs
questions.explain: Abstaining, asking for clarification, or widening the search (dropping a filter or raising top_k) are all honest responses that don't require the model to guess from weak context.
